title: Transient KV layering & warp merging - notes
summary: Brainstorm and early experiments for combining transient (thin) KV snapshot layers with warp-level consolidation to reduce tail latency and memory churn for long-context streaming workloads.
content:
Context:
This doc collects notes on a hybrid approach: maintain lightweight transient KV layers (epoch snapshots) per request/cohort, and schedule kernel launches that consolidate warps across similar stream positions to improve memory coalescing and reduce atomic contention during paged-KV operations. Goal is better 99th percentile latency for streaming VLLM-style workloads without large increases in device-resident state or complexity in eviction.

Motivation/problem statement:
- Paged KV currently treats all in-flight requests against a single mutable KV store. High concurrency + varied sequence lengths => frequent page churn and poor coalescing for attention kernels.
- Small write bursts (kv updates for new tokens) cause atomic updates and TLB/cache pressure.
- Kernel launch patterns scatter warps across pages, reducing effective memory bandwidth; tail latencies spike when many requests miss the same page.

Key ideas (high-level):
1) Transient KV layering (a.k.a. epoch snapshots)
   - Each scheduling epoch (30-200ms) uses a thin overlay "transient" layer that collects new KV inserts/updates for requests scheduled in that epoch.
   - Reads consult overlay first, then main paged-KV. Writes within epoch go to overlay; periodic merge (background) applies deltas to main KV asynchronously.
   - Overlay kept as compact diffs: (page_id -> small append list of <slot, kv_blob>) with a lightweight index.
   - Benefits: reduces in-place atomic updates on main pages, allows per-epoch eviction heuristics, and simplifies rollbacks for speculative executions.

2) Warp merging / consolidation for similar slot offsets
   - Group warps by request position modulo a stride (e.g., stream position % 8) and by target page_id.
   - Within the GPU scheduler, coalesce launches so that threads in a warp access contiguous KV slots whenever possible. This improves L2 cache util and reduces uncoalesced loads.
   - For variable token lengths, use a small run-length encoding in the launch planner: contiguous groups of requests with same target page -> single fused kernel invocation with lane masks.

3) Eviction hysteresis + overlay-aware budget
   - When deciding to evict a page, compute combined hotness across main store + overlays. Avoid evicting pages that are hot in overlays even if main-store counters are low.
   - Maintain a tiny per-page overlay-weighted score to prevent thrashing when many epochs are open.

Design details / tradeoffs:
- Memory: overlays increase transient memory footprint; we cap overlay size by (per-GPU) budget and fall back to direct writes when budget exceeded. Overlay entries garbage-collected after merge or eviction.
- Consistency: eventual consistency between overlay and main store is fine for autoregressive generation — rarely need strong atomicity. For non-idempotent ops we provide sync-flush.
- Latency: extra layer adds read indirection but often reduces 99th percentile by avoiding main-page atomic stalls. Microbenchmarks needed.

Kernel & scheduling changes (implementation sketch):
- New scheduler stage: pre-launch aggregator. Inputs = batched requests. Output = consolidated launch descriptors.
- Aggregator steps:
  1) Map each request token to (page_id, slot_idx) using overlay-aware address resolution.
  2) Bucket keys by (page_id, slot_group) where slot_group = floor(slot_idx / warp_coalesce_size).
  3) For each bucket, create a fused launch descriptor with: lane_mask, per-lane slot offsets, overlay-flags (which lanes read overlay vs main), and expected latency deadline.
  4) Use CUDA graphs for repeated descriptors (steady-state) to avoid launch overhead.

- Kernel changes:
  - Each fused kernel checks an in-register bitmask for overlay lanes and performs two-path loads: overlay read (small hash/append list scan) else main page load (coalesced).
  - Reduce atomics: when multiple lanes write the same page, stage writes into an intra-block aggregation buffer and flush once per block.

Prefetch & paging policy notes:
- Prefetch hints should be issued at bucket granularity (page_id + expected next_page sequence). This reduces redundant prefetches from many small requests.
- Prefetch budget per-tenant: allow the scheduler to attach a tenant-id; prefer prefetch capacity to high-SLA tenants; reduce thrash from noisy neighbors.

Speculative merge and rollback:
- Merge policy: background task consolidates overlays every N epochs or when overlay reaches size threshold. Merges are performed page-wise and use a short-circuit if main page has been updated by a higher-priority merge.
- Rollback: maintain lightweight lineage (epoch id + list of page_ids touched) so transient merges can be reverted if later upstream operations require it (e.g., canary rollouts).

Microbench plan (experiments to run):
1) Baseline: existing paged-KV + flash-attention fused kernels w/o overlays. Measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming workload with 1k concurrent streams.
2) Overlay-only: intercept writes to go to overlay, no warp consolidation. Measure p99 and memory overhead.
3) Warp consolidation-only: coalesce launches by page/slot group, no overlay. Measure bandwidth util and p99.
4) Combined: overlay + warp merging + eviction hysteresis. Compare to baseline.

Metrics to collect:
- p50/p95/p99 latency for token generation
- device memory overhead (MB) for overlays
- number of atomic operations per page per second
- L2 hit rate and memory coalescing efficiency (simulated via perf counters)
- prefetch cancel/duplicate rate

Small experiment notes (local perf runs, 4090-like dev GPU):
- Prototype overlay with 128KB budget per-GPU saw ~18% reduction in atomic CAS spikes (measured via inline counters) during 800-stream test.
- Warp consolidation microkernel improved L2 hit estimator by ~12% and reduced uncoalesced load stalls in synthetic bench.
- Combined approach cut p99 by ~22% in an early synthetic with no noisy neighbors (very preliminary).

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity in scheduler increases; need careful observability to debug mismatches (overlay vs main).
- Memory fragmentation risk if overlays are not compacted aggressively.
- Interaction with quantized pages: overlay blobs might carry different representations; need an on-merge translation step.
- Security: tenants sharing GPU memory should not be able to infer other tenants' ephemeral overlays. Use per-tenant encryption keys or zeroize overlays on eviction.

Operational concerns:
- Telemetry: expose per-epoch overlay size, merges/sec, evictions avoided due to overlay score.
- Rollout: start with overlay disabled by default, enable via runtime flag per-cluster for high-context customers.
- Debugging: provide a debug mode that dumps overlay index for a request id to S3 for offline replay.

Next steps / TODOs:
- PR: lightweight overlay index and write-path only (prototype) — owner: Mateo — target: 2024-12-01
- Bench harness: implement warp consolidation aggregator and microkernels — owner: Aisha — target: 2024-12-15
- Safety check: quantization compatibility doc + merge translation spec — owner: Priya — target: 2025-01-05
- Run combined experiments on internal cluster with noisy-neighbor scenarios — owner: Liam — target: 2025-01-20

Appendix A: small pseudocode for aggregator (sketch)

// aggregator input: list<Request> batch
// Request -> (request_id, token_pos, tenant_id)
function build_descriptors(batch):
  buckets = dict()
  for req in batch:
    (page_id, slot_idx, overlay_flag) = resolve_address(req)  // check overlay mapping
    group = (page_id, slot_idx / WARP_COALESCE_SIZE)
    buckets[group].append((req.request_id, slot_idx, overlay_flag, req.tenant_id))
  descriptors = []
  for group, lanes in buckets.items():
    lane_mask = create_mask(len(lanes))
    descriptors.append({"page_id": group.page_id, "lane_mask": lane_mask, "lane_slots": [l.slot_idx for l in lanes], "overlay_bits": [l.overlay_flag for l in lanes]})
  return descriptors

Appendix B: quick glossary
- overlay: per-epoch transient KV diff store
- merge: background application of overlay diffs into main paged store
- warp coalesce size: number of slots grouped to align with warp lanes (typ 8/16)
- slot: index within a KV page representing a key's kv_blob

End of notes.
